answer: One concrete mechanism: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because jade only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, marble is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any zenith approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
